## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), each Theorem 5.4 Schur generating set has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements; the paper reports verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For the in-box case \((r,n-r,i,j)=(4,5,2,2)\), \(a=b=2\), \(N=6\), and the computed \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) has rank \(6\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=6=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]
- claim-3: For the first \(r\)-boundary case outside the reported box, \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,1,1,1)\), \(a=0,b=1,N=1\); \(Q\) has rank \(1\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=1=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]
- claim-4: For the nontrivial outside-\(r\) case \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), \(a=b=1,N=2\); \(Q\) has rank \(2\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=2=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]
- claim-5: For the first \(n-r\)-boundary case outside the reported box, \((r,n-r,i,j)=(1,6,1,1)\), \(a=0,b=1,N=1\); \(Q\) has rank \(1\), no torsion invariant factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=1=N\). [artifact c888fc1cb70729a52fc6755f3631cf7884919abad2ced7ea9ef405adb67f2e99]
- claim-6: These finite torsion-free examples support, but do not prove, \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) or \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\) in all admissible cases.
## Strategy
- Treat existing finite outputs as provisional only; do not infer properties of \(Q\) until the integral presentation is justified.
- Specify admissibility and an ordering for “smallest” outside-box cases.
- Construct \(Q\) in the Schur basis of the \(r\times(n-r)\) box, impose positive-degree Pieri-action relations, and verify the relation matrix independently before Smith reduction.
- Record relation-matrix rank, cokernel free rank, complete Smith diagonal, torsion, \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)\), and \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\).
- Include a nontrivial \(n-r>5\) example with \(r\ge2\) and \(N>1\), not only the degenerate \(a=0,N=1\) boundary case.

## Gaps
- No sandbox execution or independently checked Smith certificate is supplied here.
- The identification of the previously used matrix cokernel with \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) remains ungrounded: required are the integral Schur-basis description, positive-action generators, Pieri relations, and box truncation.
- Existing artifact summaries omit complete Smith diagonals and conflate relation rank with cokernel free rank.
- The reported \(n-r>5\) boundary sample is degenerate and does not test the nontrivial conjectural range.
- Finite computations, even after validation, cannot prove universal torsion-freeness, freeness, or \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\).

## Next
- Supply the exact presentation and execute a bounded computation with independently verifiable Smith output.
- Rerun the listed samples and add a nontrivial \(n-r>5\) case.
- Preserve the conclusion as finite computational evidence only, conditional on validation of the presentation and Smith computations.
